The tachat-hashemesh refrain stands in 27 verses, and MT 2:17, 2:18, 2:19, 2:20 is its ONLY consecutive multi-verse run book-wide (sweep: 27 verses; 1 consecutive run, length 4, at MT 2:17-2:20, skeleton tier): תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.2.19, byte tier) is answered immediately by תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.2.20, byte tier) in the next row. The row lists the under-the-sun signal but never discloses that the refrain runs unbroken across its own closing edge, which under the cross-seam rule argues continuity against the row. No mark, paseq or K/Q falls in 2:17-2:19 and none is claimed — correct.

items.evidence: The quoted opener וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.20) collates at BYTE tier, verse-initial (offset 0) — the quotation itself is clean, and the row is right that savav is not shuv. Because observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of the driver, the mismatch propagates. What the span DOES carry is undeclared: תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.2.20, byte tier) and תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.2.22, byte tier) — 2 of the 27-verse tachat-hashemesh inventory (sweep: 27 verses), with 2:20 forming the tail of the unbroken MT 2:17-2:20 run that crosses this row's own opening seam. items.claim: The row's closing edge is warranted in WEB English only with no Hebrew splice, and the rejected_alternative misdescribes MT 3:1's form as the et-clause list template the bytes place at 3:2-8.
items.evidence: The opener quoted at oshb:Eccl.2.24 collates at BYTE tier, verse-initial (offset 0), and the device note's digit is right (eat-plus-drink co-occurrence: sweep: 5 verses, unit named). Two byte problems remain. First, the row's CLOSING warrant is carried entirely by the WEB rendering 'This also is vanity and a chasing after wind' at web:Eccl.2.26; the Hebrew that actually does the work, הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.2.26, byte tier — 1 of the 7-verse reut-ruach inventory and 1 of the 30 hevel-family verses; sweep: 7 verses and 30 verses respectively), is never spliced, so a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim ships with no quoted form. Second, the rejected_alternative rejects extension into 3:1 because '3:1 opens a formally distinct register (the fixed et-clause list template)'. The bytes contest the description: MT 3:1 reads לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier) — its single et governs a prepositional phrase, there is no infinitive anywhere in the verse, and it carries the book's sole occurrence of the other time-noun (sweep: 1 verse, MT 3:1, skeleton tier). MT 3:1 is a superscription, not an instance of the template, which begins at 3:2. The boundary survives on that superscription reading; the warrant as written does not.

items.claim: The setumah cited as the catalogue's opening bracket in fact TERMINATES MT 3:1, so the row's only intra-span Masoretic paragraph signal argues a 3:1 | 3:2-8 division the row denies; and the 'every line follows the et-plus-infinitive template' universal is refuted by the row's own byte-tier closing quote.
items.evidence: Mark direction, from the WLC bytes: the samekh seg keyed to Eccl.3.1 stands AFTER that verse's sof-pasuq seg and inside its own verse element — structurally identical to the pe seg that terminates MT 1:11 (the prologue poem's last verse, where the closing function is agreed). A terminating seg divides MT 3:1 from MT 3:2; it cannot open the catalogue. The inventory carries exactly 4 segs (PE at MT 1:11; SAMEKH at MT 3:1, 3:8, 9:10) and NONE terminating 2:26, so this row's opening edge has no parashah corroboration at all, while the mark it does cite falls INSIDE its span and is the one Masoretic paragraph signal available there — arguing a 3:1 | 3:2-8 split, tier-3 single-witness, against the row's own unity. Only the MT 3:8 samekh is a genuine edge bracket (it terminates 3:8 and correctly corroborates the 3:8|3:9 close, as the next row states). The staged mark validator returns GREEN because it validates the seg TYPE at the MT key, not its direction — this is a model-only defect. Second defect: 'every line follows the et-plus-infinitive template' is a universal shipped without the digit-bearing sweep the register rule requires, and it is byte-false. Of the 29 et tokens in 3:1-3:8 (independently re-tallied: 1 at MT 3:1 plus exactly 4 in each of MT 3:2-3:8 = 29 tokens over 8 verses — the row's digit is CORRECT and is a credit), 26 govern an infinitive construct, but the row's own byte-tier closing quote ends עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Eccl.3.8) — two et-slots governing bare abstract nouns, no infinitive — and MT 3:1's single et governs a prepositional phrase. 3 of 29 slots refute 'every line', and 2 of the 3 sit inside the very run the row quotes to prove the template.

(1) Its opening is subordinate, not independent: MT 3:19 begins כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי הָאָדָ֜ם (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier) — a causal subordinator whose clause depends on 3:18, which the previous row's own prose concedes introduces the comparison. (3) 'No internal restart marker' is contested at MT 3:21, which opens מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ (oshb:Eccl.3.21, byte tier) — 1 of only 4 sites for that formula (MT 2:19, 3:21, 6:12, 8:1; sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier) — and the same cluster treats the MT 2:19 instance as a row-closing verdict, so one byte formula is being read as a boundary signal in one row and as no marker at all here, with no reason given. (4) MT 3:19 carries הָֽבֶל (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier) — 1 of the 30 hevel-family verses and 1 of the 6 hakol-hevel verses (sweep: 30 verses / 6 verses, skeleton tier) — inside the span, yet observed_substrate_signals lists only the divine-name absence, leaving the strongest refrain instance in the row undeclared.
